status_values.public: A live, currently-fetchable public URL or hub reference exists; bootstrap.py may download it automatically for any profile that lists it, subject to --offline/--no-download.
status_values.manual: No automatic fetch path exists yet (source.kind='unpublished' or 'manual') -- a human must generate or place the file. bootstrap.py will never invent a URL for these; it prints the producer command or manual-placement instructions instead.
status_values.restricted: An automatic fetch path may or may not exist, but access is legally/ethically gated (derived from the restricted LLMSTU corpus, see RISK 1). bootstrap.py refuses to auto-fetch these under any profile, regardless of --offline/--no-download, and prints why.

notes: This file catalogues the artifacts the RUNTIME code path (dashboard + attention/ package) actually references by path or model id, plus the two named project-generated checkpoints and the detector checkpoint they depend on transitively -- it is not a re-listing of all 458 training checkpoints already inventoried in docs/branch_c/ARTIFACT_MANIFEST.json (that remains the fuller, audit-phase inventory of everything on disk).

verified=true means this agent computed/cross-checked the sha256 (or, for HTTP sources, the remote Content-Length and/or a content hash header) itself on 2026-08-09 without inventing any value. verified=false + sha256=null means neither was possible without a full download, which this task's rules forbid; see verification_note on each such entry for exactly what would close the gap.

redistribution.permitted uses a 3-state enum -- 'yes' / 'no' / 'pending_ethics_review' -- because several artifacts derived from the restricted LLMSTU corpus cannot be honestly marked yes or no today; [internal notes, not included] RISK 1.

destination paths are relative to cache_root, which DEFAULTS TO THE REPOSITORY ROOT ITSELF -- not a separate ~/.cache directory -- because existing runtime code (LLMDet/configs/attention_runtime.yaml, LLMDet/attention/head_pose.py DEFAULT_MODEL constants) hardcodes these exact paths relative to the repo (e.g. '../huggingface/mediapipe/...' from LLMDet/). Set LLMSTU_CACHE_ROOT only if you also intend to update those configs yourself; bootstrap.py will warn if it detects a non-default cache root combined with a profile that needs one of these path-sensitive artifacts.

demo.description: Clone and run the dashboard against already-tracked precomputed session logs (tools/dashboard/demo_session.jsonl, live_session*.jsonl) and run the deployed temporal model (checkpoint.mstcn_553_ff_s42) on CPU. No GPU, no restricted dataset, no detector.
demo.guarantees: The dashboard server starts, serves the UI, and replays a precomputed session end to end. The deployed MS-TCN checkpoint and its calibration thresholds are present and loadable. Does NOT let you point the dashboard at a new video -- that needs the detector + mediapipe + CLIP (the 'research' profile) and there is no publicly shippable sample video to try it on (see docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md).

research.description: Everything in 'demo', plus the full live pipeline (detector + tracker + CLIP + head-pose) so a researcher can run their OWN video through the pipeline end to end, on CPU or GPU, without the restricted LLMSTU dataset.
research.guarantees: Can run tools/dashboard/precompute_session.py / pipeline_bridge.py against an arbitrary user-supplied video. Cannot reproduce the thesis's own reported numbers (those require the restricted LLMSTU corpus, splits, and gold annotations -- 'full-data').

full-data.description: Everything in 'research', plus the restricted LLMSTU dataset itself (grounding_data/LLMSTU, sequence caches, splits, gold annotations) for whoever already holds institutional access to it.
full-data.guarantees: Can reproduce the thesis's reported evaluation numbers (attention/thesis_eval) and re-run the full 6-sweep checkpoint comparison. This profile's data artifacts are status=restricted: bootstrap.py will never fetch them automatically over the network -- it prints where they must be placed manually by someone with existing access.

hpc.description: Everything in 'full-data', plus the pretrained init weights and configs needed to retrain the detector or the temporal-model sweeps from scratch on a multi-GPU cluster.
hpc.guarantees: Can re-run LLMDet/tools/train.py and attention/thesis_eval/launch_sweep.py from the same init weights this project used. Training is not bit-reproducible across hardware/CUDA versions; results match within reported seed variance, not byte-for-byte. Respects this project's own 'max 4 GPUs at once' operating constraint if followed by the operator -- bootstrap.py does not launch training itself, only stages the artifacts training needs.

redistribution.note: Trained on features derived from grounding_data/llmstu_sequences_full_det, which is itself derived from the restricted LLMSTU classroom video corpus [internal notes, not included] RISK 1). The checkpoint's own weights are an aggregate statistical object (2.7M parameters trained on 4,390 sequences across 127 videos) and RELEASE_RISK_REGISTER.md does not flag model weights as a re-identification risk in the way it flags the raw per-frame annotation JSONLs -- but releasing anything trained on this corpus still inherits RISK 1's open question of whether the underlying data collection has a documented ethical/legal basis at all. This is recorded as pending, not decided, here.
